About The Role

The Director of Digital Engineering provides strategic, operational, financial, and people leadership for digital engineering services supporting Global Workplace Services. The role is accountable for service delivery, governance, innovation, lifecycle management, operational resilience, client success, and continuous improvement across smart building, workplace technology, engineering data, controls, analytics, and related digital infrastructure.

What You'll Do

Develop and execute the Digital Engineering strategy, annual priorities, operational roadmap, and performance objectives in alignment with CBRE and client business goals.
Lead the delivery and lifecycle management of digital engineering services, platforms, systems, and programs supporting facilities and workplace operations.
Provide executive oversight for building automation and controls, smart building integration, Building Orchestrator initiatives, sensors and IoT, operational technology networks, engineering data and analytics, workplace technology, remote operations, and related governance programs.
Establish service standards, operating rhythms, performance measures, controls, and continuous improvement practices that improve reliability, scalability, customer value, and operational efficiency.
Serve as the senior escalation point for Digital Engineering service risks, critical incidents, operational disruptions, cybersecurity concerns, and cross-functional dependencies.
Build and maintain effective relationships with stakeholders, CBRE leaders, operations teams, technology partners, suppliers, and vendors.
Prepare and present business reviews, performance reports, strategic recommendations, investment proposals, risk assessments, and program updates for senior leadership.
Lead resource planning, organizational design, recruitment, onboarding, coaching, succession planning, and professional development for managers and technical professionals.
Oversee budgets, forecasts, contracts, statements of work, procurement activities, vendor performance, capital planning, and operating expense management for Digital Engineering services.
Sponsor innovation and digital transformation initiatives involving automation, artificial intelligence, analytics, intelligent operations, and data-driven decision-making.
Ensure compliance with applicable CBRE and client requirements for cybersecurity, privacy, safety, service management, documentation, change control, and business continuity.
Lead by example and model behaviors consistent with CBRE RISE values while fostering accountability, collaboration, inclusion, continuous learning, and a strong safety culture.

Areas Of Responsibility And Accountability

Strategy and Transformation: Digital Engineering vision, service strategy, roadmaps, innovation portfolio, organizational change, and alignment with account and client priorities.
Operational Delivery: Service performance, reliability, operational readiness, incident escalation, business continuity, customer experience, and continuous improvement.

People and Organizational Leadership: Workforce planning, talent acquisition, performance management, coaching, development, succession planning, engagement, and leadership capability.

Performance and Reporting: Operational metrics, service-level performance, business outcomes, trend analysis, management reporting, and corrective action plans.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Analytics, Business Administration, Facilities Management, or a related discipline required.

Experience leading large-scale technology or operational programs, strategic roadmaps, organizational transformation, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Experience managing budgets, forecasts, contracts, statements of work, procurement activities, and vendor relationships.
Experience communicating complex, sensitive, or difficult information and presenting recommendations, risks, performance results, and business cases to executive stakeholders.
Working knowledge of building automation systems, smart building technologies, IoT, operational technology, digital infrastructure, analytics, automation, and service management practices.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office products, including Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Teams.
Expert organizational, analytical, financial, problem-solving, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
Ability to set and achieve targets that have a direct impact across multiple departments and functions.

Professional certification in Project Management, Lean Six Sigma, IT Service Management, Change Management, Cybersecurity, Smart Buildings, Building Automation, Data Analytics, or Cloud Technologies.

added.title: Senior Director, Engineering - Advanced Therapies
added.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Overview

Lilly is currently constructing a cutting-edge facility for the manufacture of new modalities including Gene Therapy in Lebanon, Indiana. This facility will be Lilly’s most technically advanced manufacturing site focused on the delivery of the next wave of innovative products at Lilly. It will include next-generation manufacturing technologies and advanced data collection and analysis platforms that will deliver improvements in safety, quality, and process performance. This is a unique opportunity to be a part of the team for the startup of a greenfield manufacturing site, and the successful candidate will help to start up the facility for both clinical and commercial supply. 

The Senior Director of Engineering is directly responsible for managing the site engineering function and ensuring it has the necessary capacity, capability and leadership structures in place to deliver the site engineering deliverables in support of the manufacturing plan. They provide administrative and technical leadership for the site engineering function including process engineering, process automation, maintenance, utilities, plant and project engineering, and engineering competencies.

They are a member of the Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies Site Lead Team and report directly to the Site Head. The Lead Team has collective responsibility to develop and implement the strategic direction, organizational capability and management of the site. Primarily, the members of the team drive the site toward achieving long term business objectives; they continuously develop the business and the organization for the future bearing in mind corporate objectives and the continuously changing external environment; and they manage issues that span multiple teams in the organization and extend into the broader corporate/external context.

In the project delivery phase and startup phase of the project, the Site Lead Team roles will be fluid and dynamic as we endeavor to support the project delivery, build a new organization, develop and implement the necessary systems and business processes required to support GMP operations, and build the site culture. This will require significant collaboration, creativity and resilience as the site grows to a full scale GMP manufacturing through start up.

Startup Phase

Be a collaborative, inclusive, energetic leader and support the broader lead team to:
Build the organization with the necessary capability, capacity and culture to operate this facility to the highest standards of safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Defines the site engineering priorities & roadmap in order to develop and implement the systems and processes needed to run the site. This includes leveraging existing Lilly knowledge where necessary, but also incorporating external experiences and learning.
Serve as a key member of the site HSE Lead Team, ensuring safety focus throughout project delivery and startup.
Support the project team to deliver the facility as the end user. Providing feedback and support on design decisions, commissioning strategies, startup plan, etc. Collaborate to ensure the right decisions are made to meet project deliverables and longer term strategic goals for the site.
Develop and adapt organizational structure to provide correct and capable resources and management to deliver the site to a full scale GMP manufacturing scale.
Ensure the systems are in place and executed to establish the initial qualified and safe state for equipment, processes, utilities and facilities
Build technical relationships with the relevant corporate departments and sponsors strategic corporate initiatives at a site level.

Post Startup

Continue to define and support the site engineering priorities & roadmap; integrate the functional agenda with site priorities.
Ensure the site is in compliance with corporate standards and policies for the engineering function, including applicable environmental, safety, and quality requirements.
Have external focus, benchmark best practices across network and externally
Ensure equipment, processes, utilities and facilities remain and operate in a qualified and safe state; Ensure that equipment maintenance and utilities operation are performed and documented to the highest standards of safety and quality.
Manage the site investment processes for assets (planning, prioritization, resourcing, project management, capital accounting and reporting). Own the development and delivery of the capital investment plan in accordance with the site objectives for new products, recapitalization of assets, and facility modernization.
Ensure that a robust control system exists to manage the business, identify compliance issues and escalate issues appropriately is established and maintained.
Develop the future management and technical leadership for the site and for potential global assignments.

Minimum Requirements

Minimum of a Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant Engineering discipline
10+ years of experience in a leadership role managing operations within the pharmaceutical industry, with specific knowledge and understanding of cGMPs and how they apply to manufacturing operations.
Direct experience in Drug Substance or Drug Product manufacturing.

Preferences

Must have a strong ability to form effective relationships at all levels. This candidate must be able to work closely with the Site Leadership team to ensure alignment with corporate objectives and internal decision making processes, and be able to connect and communicate effectively with all levels of the organization on site.
Should have a demonstrated track record of successfully developing, managing and executing projects from start to finish on time and within budget with high performance standards that ensure customer satisfaction.
Should have experience developing and managing extremely talented, engaged and high performing teams with a focus on building strong team cultures to ensure a safe and successful work environment.
Experience with manufacturing of advanced therapies (Biotech, Cell and/or Gene Therapy) is preferred.

At H1, we believe access to the best healthcare information is a basic human right. Our mission is to provide a platform that can optimally inform every doctor interaction globally. This promotes health equity and builds needed trust in healthcare systems. Visit h1.com to learn more about us.

H1's Product Engineering organization is the engine behind the products that put our data in front of the people who need it most, health plans, digital health companies, life sciences organizations, and the clinical teams they serve. We build the client-facing products, APIs, integrations, and intelligent workflows that transform H1's rich underlying data into real decisions: which providers belong in a network directory, where clinical trials should run, and how healthcare organizations can operate with greater accuracy and trust. Product Engineering at H1 sits at the crossroads of complex data systems and enterprise software delivery, and our work directly drives revenue, client retention, and patient impact. We move fast, we own our products end-to-end, and we hold ourselves to a high bar — because in healthcare, the quality of what we build has consequences.

What You'll Do At H1

As a Director of Software Engineering at H1, you will own a high-impact product engineering domain and lead the team responsible for the client-facing products, integrations, and workflows within it. You will set the technical vision, build and develop your team, co-own the product roadmap with the PM, and serve as the trusted engineering voice across sales, customer success, and the broader organization. You will operate with real accountability; for delivery, for your people, and for the business outcomes that depend on your domain performing at its best.

You will:

Lead, grow, and develop a high-performing product engineering team; hiring, coaching, performance management, and building a culture where engineers do their best work
Partner with Product Management to co-own the roadmap, translating client needs and business priorities into a clear engineering strategy and delivery plan
Set technical direction; architecture standards, agentic workflow practices, and the bar for what good looks like — while staying close enough to engage meaningfully in system design decisions with your team

added.description:
The APEX Power Co. Project in Hubbard, TX, currently under Phase 1 construction, is expected to expand to 1.6 GW. It features a diverse mix of generation technologies, including Siemens SGT-800/400 simple cycle turbines, MAN/Everllence 18V51/60G gas reciprocating engines, GE LM6000/LM2500 simple cycle turbines, Pratt & Whitney FT8 simple cycle turbines, and a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), enabling flexible, reliable power output. Future expansion may include additional GE aero and large frame units (6B, 7FA/7FB/7H) in simple or combined cycle configurations, allowing the plant to efficiently meet varying energy demands while supporting data center grid reliability.

Opportunity Summary

The Plant Engineering & Reliability Manager at the APEX Power Co. Project leads the site's engineering and reliability functions to support the safe, reliable, and efficient commissioning and operation of the facility. This role provides technical leadership for electrical, controls, mechanical, and plant systems; oversees engineering projects, reliability programs, capital improvements, and long-term asset strategies; and partners with Operations and Maintenance to resolve complex technical issues, improve equipment performance, and maximize plant reliability and availability.

As Plant Engineering & Reliability Manager, your responsibilities specific to the Pre-Commissioning Phase include:

Lead the site's engineering and reliability activities throughout pre-commissioning, ensuring mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, controls, and BESS systems are installed, tested, and ready for startup.
Oversee installation and commissioning of generation assets, BESS, and balance-of-plant systems, ensuring compliance with design specifications and acceptance criteria.
Manage engineering support for system turnover and startup by coordinating technical resources, resolving engineering issues, completing punch list items, and leading resolution of commissioning deficiencies, startup issues, and design concerns through Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and corrective actions.
Oversee validation of DCS, PLC, protection, instrumentation, electrical, and control systems, ensuring control logic, alarms, interlocks, communications, and data acquisition systems perform as designed before commercial operation.
Establish the site's reliability program by developing asset criticality assessments, RCM strategies, FMEA/FMECA analyses, PM/PdM programs, and equipment reliability standards before commercial operation.
Direct implementation of condition monitoring technologies, including vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, electrical diagnostics, ultrasonics, AOV/MOV testing, and online monitoring systems to establish equipment health baselines.
Ensure CMMS/EAM asset hierarchies, engineering documentation, as-built drawings, technical procedures, and reliability data are complete to support long-term plant operation.

Your scope of responsibility as the Plant Engineering & Reliability Manager includes the following primary functions:

Lead the plant's engineering and reliability programs to maximize the safety, availability, reliability, and lifecycle performance of generation assets, BESS, electrical systems, and balance-of-plant equipment.
Provide technical leadership for complex mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, controls, and plant system issues, partnering with Operations and Maintenance to improve equipment performance.
Direct RCM, PdM, FMEA/FMECA, asset criticality, and condition monitoring programs using vibration analysis, thermography, oil analysis, electrical diagnostics, ultrasonics, and AOV/MOV testing to optimize reliability and reduce lifecycle costs.
Monitor plant performance, equipment health, heat rates, reliability metrics, and operational KPIs, implementing engineering solutions to improve reliability, efficiency, and reduce forced outages.
Lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations for equipment failures, forced outages, generation losses, and significant operating events, ensuring effective corrective and preventive actions.
Manage engineering projects, capital improvements, equipment upgrades, life-extension initiatives, and plant modifications, including Management of Change (MOC), while meeting schedule, budget, quality, and safety objectives.
Oversee engineering support for planned outages, major maintenance, and long-term asset management by integrating equipment condition, operational risk, and reliability priorities into maintenance planning.
Develop and maintain engineering standards, technical procedures, equipment specifications, CMMS/EAM data, technical documentation, and plant configuration records to support safe, reliable operations.
Coordinate with OEMs, contractors, engineering firms, and corporate engineering to develop long-term asset strategies, maintenance plans, budgets, and capital forecasts.
Lead and develop the engineering and reliability team while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, regulatory, and company requirements and promoting operational excellence and continuous improvement.

Perform other duties as assigned to support safe, reliable, and compliant plant operations.

NAES Safe

Safety is a core value at NAES, and as a condition of employment, all employees are expected to remain mentally alert and work safely at all times. All NAES managers and supervisors have a direct and important role in ensuring that all work is performed in a healthy and safe manner. Effectiveness in carrying out this responsibility is part of the evaluation of each Supervisor’s performance.

Working Relationships

The Plant Engineering & Reliability Manager reports to the Plant Manager and supervises the site's engineering and reliability personnel. This role works closely with Operations, Maintenance, Environmental, Safety, and Administrative managers, partners with NAES Corporate Engineering Support Services, and provides technical leadership to support safe, reliable plant operations.

Physical Requirements And Working Conditions

Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds.

Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions.

Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. At H&P, our people are our strength.

Since 1920, Helmerich and Payne has been the industry’s most trusted partner in drilling productivity and reliability. As the world changes, so does our approach. We are changing the landscape of drilling by using cutting-edge rig technologies and drilling solutions to build upon a century of success, all while continuing to deliver better outcomes for our customers.

At H&P, our people are our strength. We strive to continually lead with our Core Values that enable employees to develop on their H&P Journey. We believe that doing the right thing means creating a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace that empowers our people to bring their authentic selves to work every day.

Some companies offer career paths. We offer a Journey of a Lifetime. Let's go far, together.

Hear directly from our employees, and leaders about their unique journeys at Helmerich and Payne.

At a Glance

The Director, Global Enterprise & Rig Technology Operations is responsible for the global operation, reliability, and security of the technology infrastructure that keeps H&P's rigs connected and the enterprise running. Leading teams across the Western and Eastern Hemispheres, the Director owns rig connectivity and network operations; datacenter, cloud, and hosting operations; rig technology platforms; infrastructure and network security operations. The role is accountable for meeting drilling-critical availability targets through global coverage, including a follow-the-sun model for appropriate functions, and will continue to integrate and standardize the combined H&P and KCA Deutag technology estate.

In doing so, the Director ensures Global IT delivers reliable, cost-efficient, secure, and scalable services that support rig automation execution, real-time rig data flow, uninterrupted drilling operations, employee productivity, and H&P's global growth.

Location:
Tulsa Office

Work Type:
Onsite

Tulsa, OK

What You Will Do

Operating model: define and execute the operating model for enterprise and rig technology services, including service placement, role clarity, global handoffs, support coverage, and consistent standards across Tulsa, Aberdeen, India, field locations, datacenters, cloud, and rig environments.
Direct global infrastructure and rig technology operations: own the day-to-day operation, availability, and performance of rig connectivity, networks, datacenters, cloud and hosting, and rig-site technology platforms across all hemispheres.
Strategic infrastructure initiatives: lead infrastructure strategy and execution for major initiatives, including global operating model transformation, international rig infrastructure upgrades, NextGen Rig Network (NGRN) capabilities, space-based connectivity, and datacenter and cloud modernization, spanning FlexRig and T-Series rigs and all operating regions.
Lead follow-the-sun operations: design and run 24x7 coverage across Tulsa (US / Western Hemisphere), Aberdeen (UK / Eastern Hemisphere), and India, including NOC rotation and third-shift coverage, ensuring seamless handoffs, on-call structures, and major-incident response for drilling-critical services.
Rig connectivity and network operations: ensure rigs, offices, datacenters, and cloud are reliably and securely linked worldwide; oversee network engineering, rig and FlexRig networking, and connectivity for remote and offshore assets.
Datacenter, cloud, and hosting operations: own core compute, storage, virtualization, backup, and cloud hosting (including Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and GCP) that underpin rig and enterprise services; drive resilience, capacity planning, and cost efficiency.
Rig technology platforms: ensure the IT and technical platforms on the rigs, including edge and OT-adjacent systems, are reliable, secure, and support safe drilling; partner closely with Digital Drilling Solutions, Digital Operations, and field operations.
Infrastructure and network security operations: keep the global network and infrastructure secure as well as available; partner closely with the CISO and Information Security on incident response, hardening, and controls, aligned with a shared follow-the-sun response model.
Governance, risk, and compliance: partner with Cybersecurity and Governance, Risk & Compliance on identity and access dependencies, network segmentation, vulnerability remediation, change control, audit readiness, and regulatory obligations.
Enterprise technology architecture: set infrastructure and platform architecture direction, standards, and governance; guide design decisions and technology selection in partnership with the principal architecture team.
Major-incident leadership: serve as the primary infrastructure leader during major technology incidents and disruptions; translate technical issues into business impact, coordinate cross-functional response, engage executive stakeholders when warranted, and ensure corrective actions and lessons learned are implemented.
Operational governance and resilience: own major-incident, problem management, and disaster-recovery readiness for infrastructure and rig technology; drive continuous improvement and reliability engineering.
Project and change governance: sponsor, approve, and govern infrastructure projects and enterprise change requests, ensuring business case, scope, funding, resourcing, vendor selection, risk management, testing, acceptance criteria, and benefits realization are sufficient before and during execution.
Executive communications: provide clear communications to IT and business leadership on infrastructure services, outages, risks, strategic tradeoffs, investment needs, and operational performance, using business language rather than unnecessary technical detail.
Post-merger integration and standardization: continue to integrate, rationalize, and standardize the combined H&P and KCA Deutag infrastructure estate toward a single global operating model.
MSP and vendor oversight: manage managed service providers and technology partners to defined SLAs and performance standards; partner with Supply Chain, who executes vendor negotiations and vendor management, providing the technical and performance requirements that inform sourcing and renewals.
Strategic vendor engagement: engage strategic vendors and managed service providers at executive and account-leadership levels to resolve issues, improve performance, manage escalations, and align roadmaps, while Supply Chain continues to execute negotiations and vendor management.
People leadership: lead, develop, and organize a global, multi-site team of managers and engineers across the Western and Eastern Hemispheres; build bench strength, on-call coverage, and succession.
Leadership standards: set expectations for managers, principals, and technical leaders consistent with H&P's job-architecture levels (for example P4, M2, M3, and M4) and coach leaders to bring recommendations, not just issues, across project engagement, incident response, change control, budgeting, vendor management, and planning.
Financial stewardship: partner with IT Business Operations on the infrastructure and platform budget, forecast, and savings, running the function with disciplined spend-to-value optimization.

What You Will Need

Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field preferred
15+ years of progressive infrastructure and operations experience, including significant leadership responsibility, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Advanced knowledge of enterprise infrastructure operations: networks, datacenter, cloud, virtualization, and hosting
Advanced knowledge of cloud platforms (Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and/or GCP) and hybrid operations
Knowledge of rig, drilling, or industrial / operational-technology (OT) environments strongly preferred
Advanced knowledge of network and infrastructure security operations and incident response
Advanced knowledge of IT service management, major incident, problem, and change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity
Advanced knowledge of enterprise technology architecture, standards, and governance
Demonstrated experience running 24x7, mission-critical operations to defined availability targets (follow-the-sun / NOC)
Ability to sponsor and govern complex programs and projects, including business case, resourcing, vendor selection, risk mitigation, acceptance criteria, and benefits realization
Experience partnering with Cybersecurity and Governance, Risk & Compliance on audit readiness and regulatory obligations
Experience managing managed service providers (MSPs) and technology partners to SLAs, including executive escalation and roadmap alignment
Proven leadership of large, geographically distributed technical teams
Experience with post-merger technology integration preferred
Financial acumen: infrastructure and platform budgeting, forecasting, and cost optimization (FinOps)
Excellent executive communication, interpersonal, and stakeholder-management skills
Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including to rig sites (passport required)

What We Offer

At H&P, our commitment to our people is at the forefront, and that includes benefits that provide employees a sense of health and financial security. We know that life continues outside of employment and actively caring of our people is our priority.

The Business Development team at Box drives partnerships and strategic initiatives that play an outsized role in differentiating and scaling Box. Strong solutions and enterprise understanding, combining an ability to map and architect AI solutions across AI, enterprise SaaS, and line-of-business platforms, skill in tactical enablement and deal support responsibilities, and a love of experimentation to turn complex partnership initiatives into actionable momentum.
Strong communication, presentation, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with comfort in both internal- and external-facing settings and the ability to establish trust across a range of technical and non-technical audiences and levels (from sellers to c-level executives).
Excel at connecting customer pain points with partner capabilities to design compelling solution narratives, with a passion for “showing, not just telling” through high-impact presentations, demos, and workshops.
Strategic, creative, self-starting mindset with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and thrive in ambiguity.

added.title: Director, Test Engineering
added.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

THE OPPORTUNITY

At Lingo, we’re building a groundbreaking health platform that combines continuous biosensor data, real-time analytics, and personalized insights to help people live fuller, longer, and healthier lives. Our systems ingest millions of sensor readings daily, powering experiences for consumers and partners worldwide, with the reliability and scalability of cloud-native, enterprise-grade platforms.

We are looking for a Director of Test Engineering to help accelerate growth across the U.S., Spain, and India. In this role, you will build and lead a world-class, globally distributed software test engineering function. The role requires a hands-on leader who thrives in building, can roll up their sleeves alongside their team, and understands that quality in a consumer health platform is both a technical discipline and a direct expression of how much we care about the people using our product.

You will own the end-to-end software testing strategy across Lingo’s platforms, mobile applications, CGM and biosensor data pipelines, AI/ML models, and the broader consumer platform. You will also grow and unify a global team of software quality engineers who operate with the same standards and urgency regardless of time zone.

What You’ll Work On

Architect and scale a distributed software test engineering team across the U.S., Spain, and India, establishing the hiring strategy, team structure, and operating model that supports Lingo’s growth trajectory.
Create a unified quality engineering culture across geographies, operating with the same standards, tools, and sense of ownership.
Define career paths, mentorship frameworks, and performance expectations that attract and retain top quality engineering talent globally.
Oversee test function staffing, resource planning, budgeting, tooling, test platforms, and third-party vendor relationships across all regions.
Own the quality architecture and test strategy across Lingo’s full technology stack, iOS and Android consumer applications, CGM and biosensor data ingestion pipelines, AI/ML inference services, and backend platform services.
Lead verification strategy for biosensor and CGM data integrity, ensuring that data flowing from wearable hardware through ingestion pipelines to consumer-facing insights is accurate, reliable, and auditable.
Build and maintain the testing infrastructure required to support continuous, high-frequency releases across mobile and platform surfaces.
Establish standards for CI/CD integration of automated test suites, ensuring quality signals are fast, reliable, and actionable for engineering teams.
Champion a shift-left testing culture, embedding quality thinking into design and development rather than treating it as a gate at the end of the cycle.
Serve as the primary engineering owner for test-related compliance activities, including audit readiness, CAPA responses, and regulatory evidence across applicable standards (IEC 62304, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR Part 11).
Partner with Regulatory Affairs and Legal to ensure test engineering practices remain aligned with applicable FDA, HIPAA, and GDPR requirements as Lingo scales internationally.
Translate regulatory requirements into practical engineering standards that the global team can implement consistently, without creating unnecessary friction in the development process.
Serve as the voice of software quality in product and engineering leadership discussions, surfacing risks, influencing roadmap prioritization, and ensuring that consumer experience software quality is a first-class consideration alongside feature velocity.
Collaborate with Product, Data Science, and Platform Engineering leaders to define shared quality standards across Lingo’s technology organization.
Build post-deployment monitoring and observability capabilities that give the team real-time visibility into quality signals in production, particularly for biosensor data accuracy and AI/ML model performance.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in software engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
12+ years in software or test engineering, including 5+ years leading and scaling engineering managers and global quality teams.
Demonstrated experience building quality engineering functions—not just running them—including hiring, org design, tooling strategy, and culture development across distributed teams.
Hands-on background in mobile quality engineering (iOS and/or Android), with experience testing consumer-facing applications at scale.
Experience with quality strategy for data-intensive platforms, including IoT, sensor data pipelines, or real-time data processing systems.
Proficient with modern automation frameworks across mobile (Appium, XCTest, Espresso), API (REST Assured, Postman, Pact), and pipeline testing.
Strong knowledge of CI/CD systems and experience integrating automated quality signals into engineering delivery workflows.
Experience owning quality compliance in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of IEC 62304, ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and related standards.
Strong executive communication skills, with the ability to represent quality engineering to senior leadership and external stakeholders across cultures and time zones.
Proven ability to lead through influence in a fast-paced, cross-functional consumer technology environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience scaling engineering teams across US, European, and Asian geographies, with sensitivity to cross-cultural leadership and distributed team dynamics.
Background in AI/ML system testing, including model validation, drift detection, and testing for probabilistic outputs in consumer health contexts.
Experience with CGM, bio-wearable, or medical device software quality, particularly where hardware and software quality intersect.
Previous experience supporting Regulatory Affairs/Quality Assurance teams during FDA or CE mark audits in a consumer health or digital health context.
Background in non-functional and performance testing tools (e.g., Locust, JMeter, Gatling, k6) applied to high-throughput consumer data platforms.

Job Description

Leads a rapidly growing, high-visibility Federal Customer support organization responsible for delivering responsive, high-quality service during critical customer events and throughout the support lifecycle. Manages managers and individual contributors while building the leadership capacity, operational discipline, and team capability required to scale successfully.

Oversees Command Center operations and serves as a senior escalation point for complex customer-impacting issues. Ensures the organization delivers timely intake, triage, issue resolution, escalation, communication, and coordination across internal teams and customer stakeholders.

Owns the operating model, staffing strategy, performance, and operational results for the organization. Partners closely with Workforce Management and leaders across Federal and Commercial Support to plan coverage, manage changing demand, respond to volume spikes, and deploy resources where they can have the greatest business impact.

This role requires a strong operational leader who can communicate clearly with senior executives and customer stakeholders, use data to drive decisions, and lead teams through fast-moving, high-visibility situations. The leader will help shape a growing organization and create meaningful development and advancement opportunities for managers and individual contributors.

Responsibilities

Customer Service and Support Advocacy:

Leads Command Center operations and customer support delivery for Federal Customers, ensuring timely, accurate, and effective service.
Serves as a senior escalation point for significant customer-impacting issues, operational risks, and complex support situations.
Establishes standards for customer engagement, issue handling, communication, documentation, and shift handoffs.
Ensures customer-reported issues are accurately documented, assigned, tracked, communicated, and resolved or routed to the appropriate technical, consulting, or product team.
Builds strong working relationships with customer stakeholders, Support Engineering, Consulting, Federal Support, Workforce Management, and other internal partners.

Problem-Solving and Resolution:

Oversees the resolution and escalation of high-impact support issues, ensuring clear ownership, timely action, accurate status communication, and appropriate handoff through closure.
Identifies recurring issues, volume drivers, operational gaps, and customer-impact trends. Leads cross-functional action plans to improve outcomes and reduce recurrence.
Coordinates with consulting, technical, product, infrastructure, quality assurance, and development teams to address complex issues and implement long-term solutions.
Ensures escalation paths, decision rights, response expectations, and communications protocols are clear and consistently followed.
Provides concise, executive-ready updates on material incidents, operational status, customer impact, risks, recovery actions, and decisions needed.

Operational Leadership and Resource Management:

Leads a growing organization of managers and individual contributors. Builds a scalable leadership structure that provides appropriate oversight, coaching, and accountability as the organization expands.
Owns staffing strategy, operational readiness, employee deployment, performance, and results for the organization.
Partners with Workforce Management to develop staffing plans, schedules, forecasts, capacity plans, contingency plans, and coverage models.
Partners with leaders across Federal and Commercial Support to align resource deployment with business needs and customer commitments.
Builds leadership capability and succession plans that support organizational growth, team development, and advancement opportunities.

Performance Monitoring and Management:

Defines and monitors operational KPIs, including contact volume, service levels, ticket intake and routing, resolution progress, backlog, escalations, customer-impact trends, and staffing performance.
Establishes real-time operational reporting and an executive update cadence that clearly communicates performance, customer status, emerging risks, key decisions, and required actions.
Uses data to identify capacity constraints, performance gaps, recurring issue drivers, and opportunities to improve staffing, workflows, and customer experience.
Leads operational reviews and converts findings into measurable improvements for customer support and service delivery.

Documentation, Knowledge, and Process Improvement:

Directs the development and maintenance of operating procedures, escalation paths, contact trees, shift handoff processes, and customer communication templates.
Ensures documentation is accurate, practical, and consistently used across the organization.
Drives knowledge management and training that prepare employees to handle customer inquiries, identify critical issues, and follow established triage and escalation processes.
Leads continuous improvement initiatives that improve the speed, quality, consistency, and transparency of support delivery.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

Leads complex operational initiatives across teams, ensuring staffing, readiness activities, timelines, risks, dependencies, and deliverables are actively managed.
Establishes and executes operating plans that support customer commitments, business priorities, resource readiness, and organizational growth.
Adjusts operational plans quickly in response to changing volumes, customer impact, staffing constraints, or business priorities.

Collaboration & Partnership:

Drives strong partnerships across Support Engineering, Consulting, Federal Support, Commercial Support, Workforce Management, Product Development, Infrastructure, and executive leadership.
Aligns teams on operating expectations, issue ownership, escalation paths, resource deployment, and customer communication.
Builds credibility with senior stakeholders through clear communication, disciplined execution, and sound judgment.

Problem Solving:

Leads teams in resolving complex operational and customer-support issues where rapid coordination and clear decisions are required.
Reviews critical issues, interprets complex data, identifies root causes, and directs actions that reduce customer impact and prevent recurrence.
Balances immediate customer needs with broader business requirements, ensuring resources are deployed where they have the greatest impact.

Continuous Learning:

Builds a team culture that values preparation, accountability, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning.
Identifies skill gaps and develops training plans that improve readiness for customer support, triage, escalation management, operational reporting, and cross-functional coordination.
Coaches managers and individual contributors to strengthen operational judgment, customer focus, data fluency, and leadership capability.

Continuous Improvement:

Leads the development and implementation of process improvements that increase the efficiency , consistency, and quality of support operations.
Uses performance data, employee feedback, customer feedback, and operational findings to prioritize improvement opportunities.
Ensures successful practices are standardized and applied across the organization.

Performance and Development:

Drives performance through clear expectations, regular feedback, coaching, and accountability aligned with Oracle performance management processes.
Develops managers and individual contributors to build a strong leadership pipeline and support career growth.
Leads hiring, talent planning, promotion readiness, and succession planning to maintain the capacity and leadership coverage required by the business.

Demonstrated experience leading customer support, service delivery, command center, contact center, or technical operations teams.
Experience managing managers and individual contributors in a high-volume, high-visibility , time -sensitive environment.
Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to communicate operational status, customer impact, risks, trends, and recommended actions to senior and executive leaders.
Strong analytical skills and experience using KPIs, operational reporting, and workforce data to make staffing and performance decisions.
Experience partnering with Workforce Management on forecasting, scheduling, capacity planning, and coverage models.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams, manage escalations, and coordinate issue resolution across technical and business organizations.
Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic environment with changing demand, competing priorities, and critical customer commitments.

added.description:
About The Role

St. Jude Children's Research Hospital is seeking an experienced and strategic leader to manage and advance the institution's research storage ecosystem. As the Senior Manager of Research Storage & Data Infrastructure within Research Information Services (RIS), you will lead the team responsible for delivering scalable, secure, and high-performance data infrastructure that supports world-class biomedical research, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and high-performance computing.

This role provides strategic and operational leadership for St. Jude's scientific computing storage environment, encompassing active research storage, archival and object storage, cloud-integrated platforms, secure research environments, data protection services, and disaster recovery capabilities. You will define technology strategy, guide platform evolution, oversee major investments, and ensure operational excellence across systems that store and protect some of the institution's most valuable research assets.

Working closely with Information Services teams, research programs, administrative leadership, and external collaborators, you will serve as a trusted advisor on storage architecture, research computing operations, service quality, capacity planning, and technology roadmaps. The position also plays a critical role in aligning infrastructure capabilities with evolving scientific and institutional priorities.

A key responsibility of this role is managing strategic vendor partnerships, including operational governance, architecture reviews, service delivery management, procurement support, technology evaluations, and performance accountability. As the primary institutional representative for research storage platforms, you will ensure effective coordination among St. Jude stakeholders, technology partners, and the broader research community.

The successful candidate will oversee infrastructure supporting AI training and inference, high-performance computing, genomics, imaging, scientific instrumentation, and other data-intensive research workloads while maintaining robust business continuity, backup, and disaster recovery capabilities for mission-critical research services.

What You Will Do:

Storage Strategy & Architecture:

Develop and manage the roadmap for St. Jude’s centralized research storage platforms, including high-performance file systems, object storage, archival storage, cloud-integrated storage, and secure research environments.
Lead architecture planning for future growth associated with AI, machine learning, scientific computing, research instrumentation, and emerging research technologies.
Evaluate new technologies and vendor solutions to improve performance, resilience, scalability, user experience, and cost efficiency.
Support institutional planning for significant increases in research data volume and complexity.

Operations & Service Delivery:

Ensure reliable operation of research storage services supporting HPC, AI, regulated research environments, institutional applications, and data-intensive science.
Establish and monitor service-level objectives, operational metrics, capacity forecasts, and performance benchmarks.
Develop reporting and dashboards to support leadership decision-making, budgeting, procurement, and lifecycle planning.
Lead incident management, root-cause analysis, change management, and continuous service improvement activities.
Document procedures and operational knowledge to support transparency and transfer across the institution and to new staff as well as updating and supporting centralized asset management and information security.

Vendor & Partner Management:

Serve as the primary relationship manager for storage vendors.
Lead governance meetings, technical reviews, architecture planning sessions, and service performance assessments.
Review equipment proposals, quotations, statements of work, and technology recommendations.
Define RACI models, escalation processes, and operational responsibilities across internal teams and service providers.

Research Data Management & Governance:

Partner with researchers, data stewards, and RIS leadership to align storage services with institutional data management objectives.
Support storage governance, archival processes, retention strategies, and lifecycle management activities.
Collaborate with Information Security and compliance partners to ensure appropriate controls for sensitive and regulated research data.
Promote data stewardship, efficient resource utilization, and sustainable storage growth.

Disaster Recovery, Business Continuity & Cyber Resilience:

Develop and maintain storage-related disaster recovery and business continuity strategies supporting institutional recovery objectives.
Ensure storage platforms are designed with resiliency, recoverability, backup, replication, immutable recovery, and cyber resilience capabilities.
Partner with Information Security, Technology Services, and RIS leadership to define recovery objectives, recovery procedures, and operational response plans.
Lead disaster recovery testing, recovery validation exercises, and documentation reviews.
Maintain architecture and operational documentation supporting audit readiness, business continuity, and disaster recovery requirements.
Identify and mitigate operational risks associated with storage infrastructure, vendor dependencies, capacity constraints, and emerging technologies.

Leadership & Team Development:

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of storage engineers, infrastructure specialists, and trusted consultants.
Foster a culture of accountability, operational excellence, innovation, collaboration, and customer service.
Support hiring, performance management, career development, succession planning, and workforce growth.
Build strong partnerships across RIS, Technology Services, Information Security, Shared Resources, and the research community.

Qualifications:

Required Education:

Bachelor's or Master's degree in business administration, computer science, data science, information science or related field.

Required Experience:

8+ years of progressive IT experience with experience managing small/mid-size teams, preferably enterprise-scale storage infrastructure, research computing environments, or large-scale data platforms.
Experience leading complex projects/delivery in terms of resources, vendors and budgets.
Experience managing teams in a supervisory/ leadership capacity, preferably 3+ years of experience leading technical teams or infrastructure operations.
Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role.

Highly Preferred Experience:

Experience managing storage technologies across on-premises, colocation, and/or cloud environments.
Experience working with storage vendors, managed service providers, or strategic technology partners.
Strong understanding of storage architecture, capacity planning, backup, replication, data protection, disaster recovery, business continuity, on-premises and cloud data storage, and performance optimization.
Demonstrated success leading operational service delivery and infrastructure lifecycle management.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred Experience:

Experience supporting high-performance computing (HPC), artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), scientific computing, or large-scale research environments.
Experience administering or supporting IBM Storage Scale (GPFS), Lustre, or comparable parallel file systems.
Familiarity with object storage platforms and S3-compatible architectures.
Experience designing and operating multi-tiered storage ecosystems spanning flash, disk, archive, cloud, and replication tiers.
Knowledge of leveraging local NVMe resources, burst buffers, caching layers, or node-local storage to accelerate AI and HPC workloads.
Experience supporting genomics, imaging, microscopy, or other high-throughput research data pipelines.
Experience with storage benchmarking, observability platforms, telemetry, and capacity forecasting.
Knowledge of disaster recovery, business continuity, cyber resilience, and data protection frameworks.
Experience supporting GPU computing, distributed AI training, and large-scale analytics platforms.

Role Summary

We are seeking an experienced, strategic leader to evolve the ServiceNow portfolio of products, associated data domains, data products, and services offered to IT, Security, and our Company's Business Divisions. The role will combine ownership of enterprise data and foundational platform capabilities with direct partnerships across Manufacturing, Research & Labs, and other business functions. The leader will stay up to date on key automation trends in the life sciences sector that center on ServiceNow; translate business priorities into a multi-year ServiceNow product roadmap; improve the quality and governance of critical enterprise data; and ensure the platform is ready to support AI-enabled workflows and future agentic capabilities.

This leader will also work closely with other leaders in the U.S. and international data products, services, and solutions organization to ensure that the organization’s needs are addressed appropriately and efficiently.

This is a highly strategic, business-facing leadership role. The successful candidate will be expected to operate beyond traditional platform delivery—shaping product strategy, challenging existing ways of working, aligning senior stakeholders, and driving measurable business outcomes.

This is a hybrid role ( 3 days/ week in office) based in Rahway, NJ.

Position Responsibilities

Role Overview:
Responsible for framing the strategic vision and enabling the efficient and effective delivery of ServiceNow platform services across business divisions and technology organizations, while ensuring that ServiceNow data is optimized, governed, engineered for scale, and leveraged for immediate analytical, business, and GenAI use cases.

Manufacturing & Business Partnership

Serve as a senior strategic partner to our Company's Manufacturing Division, our Company's Research & Labs, Animal Health and other business stakeholders.
Translate business problems into prioritized ServiceNow products and capabilities, develop roadmaps, and drive execution of prioritized initiatives.
Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior business leaders regarding ServiceNow capabilities.
Anticipate emerging business needs and proactively shape solutions with stakeholders.

AI-Ready Enterprise Data & Platform Strategy

Own the strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for ServiceNow data management capabilities, including the CMDB and related foundational data domains.
Establish ServiceNow as a trusted enterprise data and workflow platform by improving data quality, ownership, governance, completeness, accuracy and usability.
Define the future-state data model and operating approach for foundational data that enables IT, OT, asset management, enterprise architecture, security, risk and business workflows.
Lead the evolution of the CMDB toward a more federated, automated and AI-ready data foundation, including opportunities to apply automation and agentic capabilities.
Create and enforce enterprise data quality standards, ownership models, controls and remediation processes for critical ServiceNow data.
Prepare the ServiceNow data estate for AI use cases by improving semantic consistency, lineage, context, relationships and trust in enterprise data.
Partner with enterprise AI, governance, security and architecture leaders to ensure ServiceNow data and workflows can safely support AI-enabled and agentic experiences.
Partner with Enterprise Architecture, Data, Security, Infrastructure and business leaders to establish common definitions, standards and governance for enterprise data.

Product Management & ServiceNow Roadmap

Establish a product-oriented operating model across the portfolio, with clear product vision, outcomes, roadmaps, investment priorities, adoption measures and lifecycle management.
Continuously evaluate the ServiceNow product portfolio and market direction to determine what capabilities are appropriate for research laboratories, manufacturing plants, quality and compliance, security, risk and other regulated environments.
Partner closely with ServiceNow and strategic technology partners to influence product roadmaps, validate emerging capabilities, and ensure that our Company needs are represented.
Lead prioritization of demand, investment and capacity across a broad portfolio, balancing strategic transformation with sustainment and operational needs.

Team Leadership & Innovation

Lead a significant global organization spanning U.S. business-facing leadership and distributed engineering, development, testing and operations capabilities.
Build a strong leadership bench, including deputies and succession plans, to eliminate single points of failure and create scalable leadership capacity.
Establish the right balance between supplier-dependent delivery and internal ownership of sustainment and transformation capabilities.
Create a culture centered on customer service, business partnership, accountability, speed to value, and completing work across organizational boundaries.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Matrix Management:

Collaborative alignment: Proven track record of leading large, high-performing, cross-functional teams across IT, Manufacturing, Research & Labs, and Enterprise Data functions.
Enterprise representation: Confidently represent the data organization in Legal, Privacy, and Global Ethics forums to drive risk mitigation strategies.

Autonomous execution: Operates independently with a strong sense of ownership over timelines, product quality, and delivery excellence.
Financial stewardship: Highly accountable for managing budgets, driving operational efficiencies, and optimizing compute/cloud costs at scale.

Challenges the status quo: Consistently looks for ways to modernize legacy processes and embed AI-assisted workflows into standard operations.
Adaptable leadership: Navigates changing business priorities while maintaining stability and reliability for core data products.

KPMG is building a product organization designed to help transform decades of industry experience into innovative, software-powered businesses. Backed by the scale, resources, and market presence of a global network, this organization operates with the energy, ambition, and pace of a startup. We are assembling a founding team of builders, innovators, and problem solvers who are excited by the opportunity to create new products, shape new ways of working, and help define the future of technology-enabled business at KPMG. If you thrive in entrepreneurial environments, embrace ambiguity, and are motivated by the potential to make a lasting impact from the ground up, we invite you to consider joining us on this journey.

KPMG is currently seeking a Director, Platform Product Management to join our Product organization.

Responsibilities:

Shape the multi-year platform strategy and integrated roadmaps for an AI-native platform across multiple complex domains, aligning product, technology, and firm priorities
Own the capability inventory and assessment across advisory and relevant functions, identifying recurring workflows, agents, data models, and integrations that should become reusable platform assets — and harvest the best of them into the shared platform in collaboration with our engineering organization
Lead cross-domain recommendations on shared versus product-specific capabilities and build, buy, partner, or harvest options for senior product and technology leaders
Advise engineering and architecture leaders on cross-platform architecture and integration decisions, prioritize technical debt, and ensure reusable capabilities meet scalability, reliability, security, regulatory, and technical standards
Resolve major roadmap, dependency, reuse, and investment trade-offs across platform domains and product teams, using customer needs, technical feasibility, critical gaps, and platform value to guide decisions
Set platform adoption and reuse measures, using build-time, cost, reliability, and product-team outcomes; Drive internal adoption through evangelism, documentation and developer experience; Coach professionals and advance technical product-management practices across teams
Act with integrity, professionalism, and personal responsibility to uphold KPMG's respectful and courteous work environment

Qualifications:

Minimum ten years of recent experience in product management for technical products or platforms, including owning a B2B or enterprise platform product end to end
Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university is preferred; Minimum of a high school GED is required; Minimum of twelve years of equivalent professional experience is required
Proven experience shaping platform strategy across complex technical products, platforms, or processes with results in platform adoption, cross product reuse, delivery speed, cost, or customer outcomes; experience in a complex or regulated environment is preferred
Deep technical product management experience, including product lifecycle management, cross-product prioritization, analytics and experimentation, and defining non-functional requirements (NFRs) and service level objectives (SLOs). Demonstrated fluency in application programming interfaces (APIs), data models, AI and agent frameworks, integration patterns, and technical debt trade-off decisions
Demonstrated daily use of AI across working practice, and platforms or products that have shipped or shaped where AI and agent frameworks were core rather than decorative; ability to guide shared versus product-specific capability decisions and develop build, buy, partner, or harvest recommendations
Ability to operate with limited oversight, advise senior product and technology leaders, resolve complex cross-platform trade-offs, and coach professionals in leading technical product-management practices; preferred experience with developer or internal platforms (i.e. Agent orchestration, connector and integration architecture, or governed AI tooling) with audit trails and human-in-the-loop controls with application, data, or legacy modernization tooling
